newsitem.title: GERMANY: East German guards tried for horrific Wall slaying.
newsitem.headline: East German guards tried for horrific Wall slaying.

text.p: Two former East German border guards went on trial on Monday for the 1962 killing of Peter Fechter, who was shot and bled to death at the Berlin Wall as his cries for help went unheeded.

The 17-year-old Fechter, an East German mason, was shot in the pelvis while trying to climb over the Berlin Wall near an Allied checkpoint. He called in vain for help for about 50 minutes before slowly bleeding to death.
His anguished screams were ignored by the East German border guards, although West Berlin police and Western Allies tried vainly to help him by tossing first aid kits over the Wall.
Hundreds of people gathered on the western side of the Wall, who heard Fechter's cries, shouted "murderers, murderers" at the East German border guards.

The horrifying accounts of Fechter's death and dramatic pictures of East German police carrying his limp body away from the Wall were published around the world and drew widespread condemnation of the Wall and the East German regime.
Berlin's mayor places a wreath of flowers each year on August 17 -- the date of Fechter's killing -- at a cross next to the spot at the Wall where he was shot.

Although the identities of the guards were long concealed even in communist East Germany, which generally rewarded guards who shot refugees with pay and holiday bonuses, prosecutors launched an investigation in 1993 to find the names.
Prosecutors identified the men they believe were responsible as Rolf Friedrich, now 61, and Erich Schreiber, now 55.
They are facing charges of manslaughter for killing Fechter and attempted manslaughter for firing at a friend of Fechter's who managed to escape over the Wall.
Prosecutors will tell the court that Fechter and Helmut Kulbeik had been planning to flee for about five months. Both were working at a construction site in East Berlin on August 17, 1962.

During their lunch break they hid in a building near the Wall, burying themselves in a pile of sawdust before their dash to the Wall at a point just a few hundred metres (yards)from Checkpoint Charlie crossing point.

Fechter climbed through a window in the East Berlin building, jumped over a line of barbed wire and ran towards the Wall. He was just 10 metres (yards) from it when a bullet from a machine gun hit him.
Prosecutors accuse the border guards of firing without warning at Fechter. Friedrich fired 17 shots and Schreiber seven, according to records uncovered by prosecutors.

Kubleik managed to climb over the Wall unhurt. He said Fechter "stood still as if roots had grown on his feet" and leaned with his back against the Wall as if he were trying to protect himself from any more shots fired.
One possible reason East German guards did not provide first aid was that there was no senior officer on duty in that section of the Wall who had the authority to order such assistance.
The court plans to hear 26 witnesses in the case and has tentatively scheduled just two days of testimony.
